video.title: $100M CEO Explains: 7 Habits That Hold Entrepreneurs Back

summary: Codie Sanchez presents seven habits she says reduce entrepreneurs’ focus, team performance, decision quality, negotiating power and profit. She offers frameworks for protecting maker time, recognizing staff, borrowing proven systems, testing and killing ideas, prioritizing work, negotiating terms and assessing customer profitability. She also promotes her Owner Score, Growth Accelerator Workshop, advisory business and book. Most of the video is general advice and cited claims rather than a detailed account of one business.

tactics.name: Separate manager time from maker time
steps: Block the calendar according to the type of work being done.
Use roughly one-hour blocks for manager tasks such as meetings and reviews.
Protect longer, roughly four-hour blocks for deep creative or strategic work.

quote.text: So the solution is to give yourself defined time blocks by what mode you are in. Are you in manager mode or are you in maker mode?
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Recognize staff with the three Cs
steps: Give specific, individual recognition and name the work that was done well.
Connect day-to-day work to a meaningful mission.
Treat well-reasoned failures as calculated bets and recognize the effort when execution was sound.

quote.text: I call this the three C's of culture. Let me break this down.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Borrow proven systems before innovating
steps: Start with systems, benchmarks, templates and examples that have already worked.
Use roughly 80% of the approach from proven systems and reserve about 20% for experiments.
Study people who have already solved the problem before creating a new process.

quote.text: 80% of business should build from proven systems benchmarks, templates, and people who have already solved the problem.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Score ideas and set a kill date
steps: Score problem frequency, urgency, current cost and whether customers already pay for a solution from one to five.
Build ideas scoring 16 to 20; pre-sell ideas scoring 11 to 15; treat scores of six to 10 cautiously.
Set a 30-, 60- or 90-day review period and define benchmarks before proceeding.
Double down on growth, continue monitoring stable ideas, and kill declining ideas by the stated deadline.

quote.text: So basically define a period, 30, 60, 90 days. You're gonna clear benchmarks to figure out if you should keep going.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Use the 4D task filter
steps: Ask whether the task moves the business toward money or a goal; delete it if not.
Ask whether it must happen now; delay it if urgency is not real.
Delegate it if someone else can do it.
Do it immediately only when it matters, is urgent and requires you personally.

quote.text: So here's how you fix this with the 4D decision tree. Simple yes or no question.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Negotiate price and terms
steps: Treat the first offer as a starting point and ask, “Is that the best you can do?”
Negotiate terms as well as headline price, including deposits, contract length and exit penalties.
Review the five to 10 largest contracts and expenses each year.
Ask what better terms are available for an existing customer, a longer commitment or a credible alternative.

quote.text: Amateurs negotiate price. Pros negotiate terms.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Review customer profitability and fit
steps: Review customer profitability, including service effort and other costs rather than revenue alone.
Once a quarter, assess economic, behavioral, results and energy fit for each customer.
Prioritize customers who pay reliably, are easy to serve, want the work the business does best and follow its process.
Consider referring customers who are a poor fit to a competitor.

evidence_quality.rationale: This is a solo instructional video with some first-person business references, but most methods are presented as advice and many statistics are attributed only generally or without citations. The loan example is a reported client result rather than a detailed case study.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Codie promotes her Owner Score, Growth Accelerator Workshop, advisory team and book. She also recommends HubSpot and mentions a HubSpot-built scorecard tool.

extraction.review_notes: The extraction is thorough and faithful overall, and it correctly treats this as a promotional solo advice video with C-grade evidence. The main error is the 49% loan line: a garbled caption ('I've never had') was read as a first-hand claim by Codie, but in context it is the client's loan. Other fixes are a reversed buyer/supplier framing in the three-year negotiation example, a missing USD currency, the Herzberg spelling, tactic area labels outside the schema's area vocabulary, and a billing automation score for the free Owner Score that inverts the scale. The metric_claims list is padded with many trivial numbers (page numbers, clock times), but these are not factually wrong.
